title: AI UGC Tool vs AI UGC Agency: Which One Should You Pick?
summary: An AI UGC tool is software your team runs. An AI UGC agency delivers finished ads. Compare cost per accepted ad, control, disclosure and ownership.
body_markdown:
## How the options compare


Option Who does the work Published price Best when


Knowlify (agency) Knowlify's team, with a person checking every ad From $5,000 a month You want checked, finished ads and optional Meta management


Creatify (tool) Your team, using credits Standard $15 a month Someone on your team will own the workflow


Creatify Studio (managed) Creatify's creative team $100 to $200 per video You want the same vendor's managed route


MakeUGC (tool) Your team Starter $59 monthly or $29 billed yearly You want a self-serve workflow and can run retries


Arcads (tool) Your team Dollar prices not published; trial with 1,000 credits You want a trial before committing


Admiral Media (agency) Admiral's team, with human editing and review €10,000 for 20 ads up to 15 seconds You want fixed batches of scripted AI UGC


EditClub (managed) On-demand AI creative team $1,600 a month for about 60 videos You want flat monthly volume without creators


Prices are as of October 2026. Confirm each one before you compare, because each provider prices a different unit.


## When an AI UGC tool is the right choice


A tool fits when someone on your team already writes hooks and scripts, can judge product accuracy and has time to run the retry loop. It also fits when you want to learn the format before committing to a managed service. Keep the first test small and log every regeneration.


Plan for credits. Every generated retry draws on credits, so count retries as cost. On MakeUGC's Starter plan, 500 credits at 100 per talking-actor generation covers about five generations before any rejected takes, which is simple arithmetic from the published figures.


Tools also stall at approval. A tool can produce many versions quickly, but someone still has to decide which one matches the approved product facts, and no tool makes that call for you.


## When an AI UGC agency is the better buy


An agency fits when your marketer, founder or media buyer is the bottleneck. If you are rewriting scripts, operating generators, editing exports and chasing approvals each week, that time can cost more than the agency quote. Our[DIY cost comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/diy-ai-video-ads-vs-done-for-you) shows how to count it.


Ask for the quote to list ads per month, length, revision rounds and campaign scope on separate lines, because those lines are where quotes differ. Check whether campaign and budget management are included, since Admiral Media, for example, agrees those separately.


## Disclosure, ownership and a two-step test


Disclosure and claim rules apply to both routes. As of October 2026, the[FTC's testimonial Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false. Hiring an agency does not remove your responsibility for what the ad says, so keep approval of every claim with your team.


Platforms add their own rules.[TikTok's advertising policy](https://ads.tiktok.com/resources/help/article/tiktok-ads-policy-misleading-and-false-content) requires disclosure for fully AI-generated or significantly AI-modified content.[Meta's transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) says it labels ads with a photorealistic AI-generated person when its own generative tools create or significantly edit the ad, and it says it will begin detecting third-party tools without saying that detection is live.


Ownership is a contract term. Ask every provider who owns the source files, generated presenters and scripts, and whether you keep the right to reuse them after the contract ends. Then run a two-step test: send the same brief to a tool and to an agency, log hours, retries and accepted ads, and compare cost per accepted ad with the formula in our[DIY cost comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/diy-ai-video-ads-vs-done-for-you) . For a broader list of options, see our[AI UGC tool alternatives guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-ugc-tool-alternatives-for-brands-spending-10k-50k-mo-on-meta) .


## Key takeaways


- A tool suits a team that will own scripts, generation, review and approvals.
- An agency suits a brief where production or approval time is the bottleneck.
- Count retries and review hours as cost in both routes.
- Agree ownership of source files and approve every claim before rendering.
- Keep the scope of the agency quote on separate lines for ads, revisions and campaigns.


## FAQ


### Is an AI UGC tool cheaper than an agency?


It can be cheaper on the invoice and more expensive in total when someone spends the week generating, retrying and exporting. Compare the subscription plus your team's hours with an agency quote for the same accepted ads. Count only the ads that pass your acceptance list.


### Can I move from a tool to an agency later?


Yes, if your scripts, approved product facts and source files stay in a folder you control. Ask the agency which of those files it can reuse, and check the tool's contract for export and ownership terms before you leave it.


### Do AI UGC ads need a disclosure label?


Often. TikTok requires disclosure for fully AI-generated or significantly AI-modified content, and Meta labels some ads with photorealistic AI-generated people. Check each platform's current rules before you upload, whichever route you choose.


### Can an AI presenter run ads from its own account?


No.[Meta's partnership ads documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/ad-creative/partnership-ads) describes partnership ads as ads run from a creator's or partner's handle, and a generated presenter has no handle of its own. Creator-handle ads need a real creator.
